note: Review pass 8 of the undescribed mobile-app-ui images. Sheets review_09.jpg and review_10.jpg. Written from the processed web images. Palette, dimensions and contrast are measured elsewhere.

IMG-0379.title: Banking home - balance and transactions in light mode
IMG-0379.description: A light personal-banking home screen. The header has a small avatar, a chevron and a pair of icon controls; beneath it a large balance figure sits with an eye toggle. A row of small action pills follows, then a compact 'Transactions' section with grouped entries - each a name, a date and a signed amount - and a tab bar at the foot. The composition is deliberately plain, and that is the reference: with one large numeral, one row of pills and one list, the screen communicates the three things a banking home must, in strict order of importance.
IMG-0379.quality: Clear capture; the balance and transaction rows are legible.

IMG-0380.title: Banking home - dark variant of the same layout
IMG-0380.description: The dark counterpart of IMG-0379, showing the identical structure - avatar header, large balance with an eye toggle, action pills, grouped transactions, tab bar - rendered on a near-black surface with a soft violet glow behind the balance. Filed as its pair because the two together demonstrate what a dark mode should actually change: surfaces and glow only, with every dimension, label and order of elements held constant between the two.
IMG-0380.quality: Clear capture; the balance and transaction rows are legible.

IMG-0381.title: Travel app - three screens with an orange accent
IMG-0381.description: Three light travel screens shown side by side, unified by a single orange accent. The left is a home view with a greeting, a search block and a list of feature rows; the middle is a details screen with a photograph of a destination and an information card floating over it; the right repeats the home structure with different content. The set is a good demonstration of accent discipline: orange appears only on the primary buttons, one active tab and a single highlight per screen, so the three views feel related without any of them looking orange.
IMG-0381.quality: Clear capture; the three screens are legible.

IMG-0382.title: Orange app - a twelve-screen screen-sheet
IMG-0382.description: A sheet of roughly a dozen screens from one product, all sharing a warm orange-and-white palette. The screens cover a home view, list views, a detail page, a form, a profile, a settings panel and several modal states, each labelled beneath. The sheet is a reference for range: it shows the same design language applied across the whole surface area of a product, which makes it easy to check whether the type ramp, corner radius and accent are genuinely reused or merely similar.
IMG-0382.quality: Clear capture; individual screens are small but the structure is readable.

IMG-0383.title: Fitness app - a seventeen-screen screen-sheet
IMG-0383.description: A large sheet assembling seventeen screens from a single fitness product, arranged in a grid of five columns with each screen labelled underneath. The set spans onboarding, workout logging, progress charts, a medication or dose tracker, profile and settings. Filed as a completeness reference: at this scale you can see whether the product has one consistent card style across every surface, and whether the accent is used for meaning or merely for colour.
IMG-0383.quality: Clear capture; the grid is dense but each screen is identifiable.

IMG-0384.title: Dose Logged - a green confirmation with a burst badge
IMG-0384.description: A pale green confirmation screen centred on a starburst badge containing a check, with the words 'Dose Logged' above it and a short encouraging line beneath. A row of small reaction buttons follows - including a green check - and a large solid 'Done' button closes the screen. The screen is a clean example of a positive confirmation: a single symbol, one sentence and one way out, with the soft green wash stating success before any text has been read.
IMG-0384.quality: Clear capture; the headline and button label are legible.

IMG-0385.title: Vitals app - 'Vitals Logged' on a green field
IMG-0385.description: A light vitals-tracking screen headed with a back control, a title and a search icon. The body centres on a large green starburst badge holding a check, with a short congratulatory line beneath it, followed by a row of small circular reaction buttons and a large green primary button at the foot. The screen is nearly identical in structure to IMG-0384 but on a tinted field rather than a coloured card, which shows how far a background wash alone can carry the same confirmation pattern.
IMG-0385.quality: Clear capture; the badge and button label are legible.

IMG-0386.title: Health monitor - blood pressure, blood sugar and ECG
IMG-0386.description: Three light health-monitoring screens shown side by side. The first is a blood-pressure view with a reading, a line chart over a date range, a small annotation and a short parameter list; the second is a blood-sugar view with a reading, a soft blue illustration and a set of reference ranges; the third is an ECG trace rendered as a bright waveform on a pale blue field with accompanying text. The set is a strong reference for clinical data presentation: consistent header, one large reading, one chart, and restrained colour reserved for the trace itself.
IMG-0386.quality: Clear capture; the readings and chart shapes are legible.

IMG-0387.title: Shop smarter - three-screen violet onboarding
IMG-0387.description: Three light screens from a shopping product, staged as a row over a violet gradient backdrop with soft floating 3D shapes in the corners. The left is a splash with a headline and a violet button; the middle is a profile or account screen with grouped rows and a violet action; the right is a checklist of tips under a heading, each row with an icon and a label. The staging is the notable part - the lavender field and the small 3D props give an otherwise plain set of utility screens a distinct mood.
IMG-0387.quality: Clear capture; the three screens and their labels are legible.

IMG-0388.title: Amazon Prime - dark perks screen with a yellow banner
IMG-0388.description: A dark Amazon Prime perks screen. The header carries a greeting and a date. A wide banner card in bright yellow states a renewal date with a bold line and a pill button, and is the only saturated element on the page. Below it sit grouped sections - a 'Favourite carousel' shelf and a 'Watchlist' shelf - each with small square thumbnails and short labels, above a tab bar. The screen is a textbook example of a single high-contrast banner used to carry the one piece of transactional information, with everything else kept dark and quiet.
IMG-0388.quality: Clear capture; the banner text and shelf labels are legible.

IMG-0389.title: Ride app - $30.00 charge with saved places
IMG-0389.description: A dark ride-hailing screen showing a receipt or account view. A balance-style figure of $30.00 sits at the top with a small icon row beside it, followed by a card naming the user's personal details and a 'Saved Places' list - Home, Work and a named address - each with an icon, a label and an address line. A payment method row closes the list above a tab bar. The screen is a useful reference for a saved-places pattern: three persistent rows with clear labels remove almost all address typing from the ordering flow.
IMG-0389.quality: Clear capture; the figure and place labels are legible.

IMG-0390.title: Social feed - dark post with a photographic card
IMG-0390.description: A dark social feed screen. A header row carries an avatar, a name and a time; beneath it a short block of post text, then a large rounded photo card showing a city street at dusk, followed by a row of engagement counts and a short comment list with small avatars. A composer bar is fixed at the bottom. The screen is a solid reference for a media-first feed item: the photograph is given a generous corner radius and full column width, while every piece of text around it is small and low-contrast so the image remains the item.
IMG-0390.quality: Clear capture; the post text and photo card are legible.
